description: Content source registry — the closed vocabulary of WHERE a piece of patient voice originated. Parallel to indications and burdens as a cross-cutting axis. Each segment, quote, or ingested content row carries one content_source_id FK into this registry. Distinct from registries/sources.json, which is dataset PROVENANCE (how data got into the system: manual extract, primary research, third-party provider). A YouTube transcript can be content_source: 'youtube_transcript' AND dataset source.type: 'third_party_provider' — different axes.

items.label: Interview transcript
items.description: Structured one-on-one or focus-group interview. Long-form, question-scaffolded; supports turn-by-turn attribution, structured demographics, and the analyst-curated coding pipeline. The original JourneyMapper content type.

items.label: Social media post
items.description: Short-form post from a public social platform (Reddit, X / Twitter, Facebook, Instagram, TikTok caption). Author is typically pseudonymous; engagement signals (likes, replies, shares) often available. No question scaffolding; topic-mapping via embedding match is the primary annotation path.

items.label: Social media comment
items.description: Reply to a social media post. Same platforms as social_post but distinguished structurally — comments share a post_id with their parent and inherit thread context. Annotation paths mirror social_post; weighting may differ.

items.label: YouTube transcript
items.description: Auto- or human-generated transcript of a YouTube video (creator vlogs, patient testimonials, advocacy organization channels). May include multiple speakers; timestamps are usually retained. Public-figure attribution is the norm.

items.label: Forum / community post
items.description: Post or comment from a patient-community forum (Inspire, HealthUnlocked, PatientsLikeMe, Mumsnet health boards, condition-specific Facebook groups). Pseudonymous, often deeper threaded discussion than open social platforms.

items.label: Forum / community comment
items.description: Reply to a forum_post. Inherits thread context from its parent; commonly carries reply-depth and quoted-text affordances absent from social platforms.

items.label: Blog post
items.description: Long-form first-person blog entry (Medium, personal websites, advocacy organization blogs). Patient or caregiver authored. Less ephemeral than social posts; often more reflective and narrative.

items.label: Blog comment
items.description: Reader comment on a blog post. Public attribution varies (name + URL, pseudonym, anonymous). Distinct from forum_comment in that the parent narrative is the original post, not a multi-author thread.

items.label: Search query
items.description: Anonymous or aggregated search query string (from search-volume providers, autocomplete data, or panel-based query logs). The smallest unit of patient voice — no surrounding narrative, only the question or phrase being searched.

items.label: Podcast transcript
items.description: Transcript of a podcast episode (patient story podcasts, condition-specific shows, advocacy podcasts). Multi-speaker, often long-form. Public-figure or pseudonymous attribution depending on the show.
